soap.subjective: Client reports sudden panic surge during quarterly budget review. Heart rate 110 bpm, fear of catastrophic failure.
soap.objective: Affect congruent with anxiety. Mild psychomotor agitation. Denies suicidal ideation. GAD-7: 14.
soap.assessment: Perfectionistic coping schema triggering sympathetic flight-or-fight response under evaluation.
soap.plan:
1. Introduce thought record diary.
2. Physiological sigh technique for acute panic.
3. Session 6: Behavioral delegation experiment.

notes.title: Weekly Reflections: Decatastrophizing & The Physiological Sigh
notes.content:
Key Insights from Today's Session

Remember that a spike in heart rate during a high-stakes meeting is simply your body's sympathetic nervous system gearing up for performance—it is not evidence that you are failing.

Your Action Homework for the Week:

  • The 2-Breath Physiological Sigh: Two quick inhales through the nose followed by one long, slow sigh through the mouth whenever you notice muscle tension.
  • Thought Record Journal: When an anxious thought arises ("They will realize I don't know this"), write down:
    1. What is the worst that can happen?
    2. What is the most likely outcome based on past experience?
    3. If my closest friend had this thought, what compassionate advice would I offer them?

Be gentle with yourself this week. You are building new neural pathways!

notes.title: Session 3: Dual Process Model of Bereavement

soap.subjective: Client discussed wave of guilt when laughing at a social event last weekend. Recalled feeling disloyal to deceased parent.
soap.objective: Tearful during loss narrative. Good insight and emotional responsiveness.
soap.assessment: Oscillation between loss-oriented and restoration-oriented coping is natural. Normalization provided noticeable relief.
soap.plan: Continue grief narrative processing. Introduce memory ritual before bed to mitigate evening rumination.

notes.title: Grief & Permission to Experience Joy
notes.content:
Remember:

Grief does not shrink over time; rather, our lives expand around it. Feeling moments of lightness, laughter, or engagement in your art is not a betrayal of your memory—it is how your spirit rests and heals.

Gentle Reflection Prompt:

Whenever grief feels heavy, light a small candle or take 3 deep breaths and write one thing you are grateful your parent shared with you.

notes.title: Cognitive Defusion: You Are Not Your Thoughts
notes.content:
Mindset Shift: Cognitive Defusion

Instead of saying "I am inadequate at managing this team," practice saying "I notice my mind is generating the thought that I am inadequate." Notice the space between the observer and the thought.

Weekly Action Experiment:

  • Identify one task this week where "80% good enough" is sufficient, and deliberately submit it without secondary revisions.
  • Notice what physical sensations arise, breathe into them, and do not scramble to fix.

notes.title: Session 4: Values Clarification & Defusion from Impostor Thoughts

soap.subjective: Client reports exhaustion from masked ADHD symptoms at work. Feels constant pressure to over-deliver.
soap.objective: High verbal cadence, animated affect. Insight intact. Good rapport.
soap.assessment: Fusion with belief "If I rest, I am lazy". High cognitive avoidance of uncomfortable emotional states.
soap.plan:
1. Introduce ACT "Leaves on a Stream" defusion exercise.
2. Implement 25-minute Pomodoro pacing with mandatory screen-free breaks.

notes.title: Somatic Grounding & Anchoring
notes.content:
5-4-3-2-1 Sensory Reset

Whenever your thoughts pull you into rumination about the future, pause and name:

  • 5 things you can see around you
  • 4 things you can physically feel (feet on floor, clothes on shoulders)
  • 3 things you can hear
  • 2 things you can smell
  • 1 thing you can taste

This anchors your nervous system back in the objective present moment.

notes.title: Session 3: Attachment Protest Behaviors & Emotional Regulation

soap.subjective: Client reported recognizing defensive withdrawal pattern during conflict over holiday planning.
soap.objective: Demonstrated increased reflective capacity. Acknowledged underlying vulnerability.
soap.assessment: Anxious-avoidant relational dynamic. Client reacts to perceived disconnection with immediate pursuit or protest.
soap.plan:
1. Role-play expressing soft primary emotions ("I feel scared") rather than secondary anger.
2. Agree on a mutually accepted 15-minute cool-down ritual.

notes.title: Identifying Primary vs Secondary Emotions
notes.content:
Soft Vulnerability vs Hard Defensiveness

When disagreements happen, our defensive armor (anger, blame, sarcasm) shows up first. Beneath that armor is usually a tender primary emotion: fear of rejection, sadness, or a longing for closeness.

Communication Homework:

Use the simple formula: "When [event] happened, I felt [primary soft emotion], because I value our connection."

notes.title: Session 2: Boundary Setting Without Excessive Justification

soap.subjective: Client felt intense guilt after saying "No" to hosting relatives during festival weekend.
soap.objective: Affect brightened as session progressed. High willingness to explore self-compassion.
soap.assessment: Family system enmeshment where boundaries were historically treated as personal rejection.
soap.plan:
1. Practice concise, respectful boundary statements without over-explaining.
2. Journal feelings of guilt as "growing pains" rather than wrongdoing.

notes.title: Setting Clear & Loving Boundaries
notes.content:
Healthy Boundaries Are Kindness

A boundary is not a wall to push people away; it is a clear door with a lock so you can welcome others without depleting yourself.

Clean Boundary Scripts:

  • "I love you and want to spend time together, but I am unable to host this weekend."
  • "I need downtime this evening to recharge. Let us catch up on Sunday."

Notice that you do not need to invent excuses. A simple, gracious statement is enough.
